stem.en: After 10-15 days, roots have grown on a buried lemon twig. What should the gardener do next?

text.en: Bury the rest of the twig, tip and all.

feedback.en: Burying the leafy tip does not help. The twig is ready to stand alone.

text.en: Cut the twig from the parent plant.

feedback.en: Yes. With its own roots, the twig can grow as a new plant.

text.en: Dig up the roots and throw them away.

feedback.en: The new roots are what the twig was waiting for. They must stay.

text.en: Graft the twig onto a wild lemon.

feedback.en: Grafting is another method. Layering ends with cutting the twig free.

explanation.en: Layering ends when roots have developed from the buried part. Then the twig is cut from the parent, and it grows as a new plant.

hints.en: What was the twig waiting for?
Once it has roots, does it still need the parent?
